newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to firm on back of Dow, Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to firm on back of Dow, Chicago.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to firm on the back of a steep rise on Wall Street and in Nikkei futures in Chicago overnight, brokers said. But profit-taking pressure is intense above 18,000 on the Nikkei average and gains will likely be watered down by the close, they said.
On Tuesday, the Nikkei average of 225 leading shares climbed 241.12 points or 1.36 percent to finish at 17,933.59. Its June futures added 320 points to 17,960.
"In the morning, Nikkei futures and blue chips will respond to the U.S. stocks' surge," said Osamu Yamazaki, New Japan Securities Co Ltd director.

The Dow soared 135 points or 2.1 percent to close unofficially at 6,587, helped by a report showing a weaker-than-expected increase in the March consumer price index. June Nikkei 225 futures surged 340 points to end above the 18,000 threshold at 18,080.
Brokers said that apart from the cues coming from the U.S. markets, there was little to give direction to trade in Tokyo.
Eyes would be on blue chips, some of which are nearing the end of their recent rally, and what investors will buy instead.
Whether or not the short-covering spree in bank shares will continue is another point of concern, brokers said.
